panels.title: Films
panels.description:
Films with a file on disk. Radarr's list is longer than this by whatever it is still
hunting for; those show up in "Waiting on Radarr" below rather than being counted here,
so this number is what you can actually play tonight.

panels.title: Series
panels.description:
Series with at least one episode on disk. A series Sonarr is monitoring but has no file
for is not counted.

panels.title: Episodes
panels.description:
Episode files across every series. The count Sonarr itself reports, so a season pack that
landed as twelve files counts twelve.

panels.title: Recent quality upgrades
panels.description:
Files replaced by a **different** quality, newest first.

An upgrade is two events at the same instant: the old file deleted with reason `Upgrade`, and the new
one imported. The same quality on both sides means it was a custom-format score upgrade, not a
resolution change.

**Colours follow the download policy, not the resolution:**
🔵 4K · 🟢 what the TV direct-plays (Bluray/WEB 1080p) · 🟠 works but wastes space (Remux-1080p, 720p)
· 🔴 unwanted (BR-DISK, cams, SD)

panels.title: Upgrades tracked
panels.description:
How many upgrades are currently being exposed. The exporter keeps only the most recent ones, so
this is a window, not a lifetime count.

panels.title: Upgraded in the last 7 days
panels.description: Upgrades whose timestamp falls inside the last week, out of the window the exporter keeps.

panels.title: Stuck on a bad quality
panels.description:
Titles whose current file is a quality the download policy rejects: cams, telesyncs, SD, DVD,
BR-DISK.

Worth checking by hand, because Radarr does not always treat these as upgradable. A quality that is
not even allowed in the profile has no rank to compare against, so it can sit below the cutoff
without ever appearing in the upgrade list.

panels.title: Waiting on Radarr
panels.description:
Everything Radarr is waiting for, and what it is waiting for.

| Kind | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| 🔵 `downloading` | in the queue right now. **Expected** is the ETA, or `stalled` when no bytes have moved |
| 🟠 `missing` | monitored with no file at all: cannot be watched |
| 🟢 `upgrade` | watchable, but below the profile cutoff |

**Now** is the quality on disk, 🔴 `none` when there is no file.

**Expected** is the honest half of "when". Nobody can say when someone uploads a good release, but
two things are knowable:

- `in cinemas, no digital date` — the film has no home release yet, so no amount of searching will
  find a better one
- `out, waiting for a good release` — it exists in the world, so this is down to an indexer carrying
  it. The nightly cutoff search asks about exactly this list

panels.title: Reachable
panels.description:
Whether the exporter can talk to qBittorrent's WebUI at all. Down means the metrics on this row
are stale, not that the torrents stopped.

panels.title: Torrents in error
panels.description:
Torrents in `error` or `missingFiles`: the data is unreadable, or it was moved or deleted from
under qBittorrent. These never recover on their own.

panels.title: Stalled downloads
panels.description: Torrents that want to download but find no seeds. qbit-manage removes one 12 hours after its last byte, so what shows here is the window before that: blocklist it in Radarr if you want another release searched for sooner. The alert only fires if one is still here after a day, which means the cleanup itself stopped working.

panels.title: Torrents
panels.description:
**What the states mean**

| State | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `downloading` | pulling data right now |
| `metaDL` | fetching the .torrent metadata (magnet just added) |
| `stalledDL` | wants to download but finds no seeds: stuck |
| `queuedDL` | waiting for a download slot |
| `uploading` | sending data to someone right now |
| `stalledUP` | seeding, but nobody is downloading from you. Normal for old titles |
| `queuedUP` | finished, waiting its turn to seed. **Not seeding at all** |
| `pausedUP` / `stoppedUP` | stopped on purpose, or its share limit was reached |
| `checkingUP` / `checkingDL` | verifying pieces against the disk |
| `moving` | being moved between folders |
| `error` / `missingFiles` | broken: the data is unreadable or gone |

Many torrents sitting in `queuedUP` means qBittorrent's active-torrent limit is lower than the number
of torrents, so it is rotating them. Queued time does not count towards a share limit, so those
torrents also take longer to retire themselves.

Keyed by infohash, not by name: cross-seed gives every copy of a release the same name, and joining those on the name merged two torrents into one row of mixed numbers.

panels.title: Torrents by state over time
panels.description:
How the mix of states moves. What to read into it:

- `queuedUP` above zero means the active-torrent limit is below the number of torrents
- `stalledUP` falling means torrents are reaching their share limit and stopping, which is the
  library cleaning itself up
- `stalledDL` that never clears is a dead release
